cards.text: It's the night of the Last Supper, and Jesus is still talking with His disciples, His closest followers. He paints them a picture: 'I am the true vine.' And friend, every vine needs somebody looking after it.

cards.question: Jesus is the true vine. Who does He say is the keeper of the vineyard?

cards.text: Now the keeper goes to work on the branches. Every branch in Jesus that bears no fruit, He cuts off.

cards.question: The keeper of the vineyard leaves the branches that bear fruit alone.

cards.text: Pruning sounds a little scary, friend. But Jesus has good news for the disciples: they're already clean.

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples, "You are already clean because of the ___ I have spoken to you."

cards.text: Then Jesus starts saying one word over and over: remain. 'Remain in Me, and I will remain in you.'

cards.question: Jesus says a healthy branch can bear fruit by itself, even apart from the vine.

cards.text: Then Jesus says it plain: 'I am the vine and you are the branches.' The one who remains in Him, and He in him, will bear much fruit.

cards.question: And apart from Jesus, what does He say the disciples can do?

cards.text: I spent years in a junk drawer and stamped exactly ZERO cookies, so I am NOT arguing with that one. Then Jesus says anyone who doesn't remain in Him is like a branch that is thrown away and withers.

cards.question: What does Jesus say happens to withered branches like that?

cards.text: Then Jesus makes a promise about asking, for the ones who remain in Him. And this is NOT a 'your call is important to us, please hold' kind of promise.

cards.question: Jesus says that if the disciples remain in Him and His words remain in them, whatever they ask will be done for them.
Jesus says something brings His Father glory. What is it?

answers.text: That they build a great temple

cards.question: Bearing much fruit proves the disciples are Jesus' ___.

cards.text: Now Jesus talks about love. 'As the Father has loved Me, so have I loved you.'

cards.question: Right after saying He loves the disciples the way the Father loves Him, what does Jesus tell them to do?
How does Jesus say the disciples will remain in His love?

answers.text: By praying three times a day

cards.question: Jesus says He Himself has kept His Father's commandments and remains in His Father's love.

cards.text: Then Jesus tells the disciples why He's been telling them all this.

cards.question: Why does Jesus say He has told the disciples these things?

answers.text: So His joy may be in them and theirs be complete
So they will not be afraid of the crowds again
So they can teach in the synagogues tomorrow

cards.text: Then Jesus gives them His commandment. One line. No fine print.

cards.question: "This is My commandment, that you love one another as I have ___ you."

cards.text: Then Jesus tells them what the greatest love looks like.

cards.question: What does Jesus say is the greatest love anyone can have?

answers.text: Laying down his life for his friends

cards.text: Friend, my idea of a big sacrifice is handing a baker the LAST chocolate chip. Then Jesus tells the disciples who His friends are.

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples they are His friends if they do what He commands them.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, 'No longer do I call you servants.' Baker, that is a PROMOTION, and nobody even had to fill out a form.

cards.question: Jesus explains the difference: a servant does not understand what his ___ is doing.
Jesus calls the disciples friends because He has made known to them everything He learned from His Father.

cards.text: Then Jesus settles a question about who chose whom.

cards.question: The disciples chose Jesus first, and then He chose them.
What did Jesus appoint the disciples to go and do?

cards.text: And Jesus says it one more time: 'This is My command to you: Love one another.' Stick around, friend, because Jesus isn't done talking to them tonight.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 6 quotes "You are already clean because of the ___ I have spoken to you.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 8 quotes "This is My commandment, that you love one another as I have ___ you.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card states facts from outside the passage: that it's the night of the Last Supper and that Jesus is still talking with His disciples (John 13:1-2, 13:30). The card cites only John 15:1 and gives no reference for those facts.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: No card tells why the keeper prunes the fruitful branches: "to make it even more fruitful" (John 15:2). Card 4 only establishes that he doesn't leave them alone, and card 5 moves on. The baker leaves without the reason for the pruning.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to fill in the exact wording of Jesus' line ("word") with nothing earlier that points to it. "Blessing" and "prayer" are also things a person speaks, so this is a guess at unseen wording rather than reasoning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The setup gives away card 14's true-or-false answer. Card 13 says Jesus makes a promise about asking and that it's NOT a 'please hold' kind of promise. That tells the baker that whatever they ask will be done, so the statement on card 14 can only be True.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The question already contains the right answer: "proves the disciples are Jesus' ___" with "disciples" as the answer. The right answer stands out because it repeats a word from the question, so the card tests nothing.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: Several story cards in stop 2 are stripped down to plain narration with none of Papa Dorin's voice. Card 1 ("Now Jesus talks about love."), card 5 ("Then Jesus tells the disciples why He's been telling them all this.") and card 9 ("Then Jesus tells them what the greatest love looks like.") read like flat setup lines, not the storyteller.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: No card covers the second half of John 15:16: "so that whatever you ask the Father in My name, He will give you." Card 18 asks only about bearing fruit, and card 19 moves on to verse 17, so the baker misses the promise about asking the Father in Jesus' name.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
